Exercise: Jumping Chin Up with Drop Landing (LIFTMOR)
Pattern: Vertical pull: pull up / chin up / hangs
Muscles: Lats, upper back, biceps, grip, core
Why: Used in the LIFTMOR trial for postmenopausal bone health: jump to the top of a chin up, lower slowly, then drop and land firmly on both feet. The landing impact loads the hips and spine. Supervised Teams only, screened, no pelvic floor symptoms.
Cue 1: Grip slightly wider than shoulders (chin up: palms facing you)
Cue 2: Pull the shoulder blades down first, then drive the elbows to the ribs
Cue 3: Chin over the bar, lower slowly to straight arms
Common faults: Kipping or swinging; Half reps; Shrugging at the bottom
Progress to: Weighted Pull Up (G4); Weighted Chin Up (G4); Commando Pull Up (G4)
Progress by: Band assisted → negatives → bodyweight → weighted
Regress to: Hanging (Supported) (G2); TRX Assisted Pull Up (G2); Band Assisted Pull Up (G2)
Regress by: Lat pulldown, TRX assisted pull up, scapula pull up, dead hang
Same level swaps: Pull Up; Chin Up; Dead Hang
Joint notes: Shoulder pain: neutral grip, band assistance. Hanging can irritate some shoulders: build up gradually.
Default prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8 or total reps
Group alternative: Use a no impact exercise from the same pattern

Muscles: Calves (gastrocnemius straight knee, soleus bent knee), Achilles
Why: Rise onto the toes and drop firmly onto the heels. A low level impact progression used to load bone in members not yet ready for jumps. No flight phase, so it can be used in groups if comfortable.
Cue 1: Full stretch at the bottom
Cue 2: Rise to the highest point on the big toe
Cue 3: Pause, lower slowly (3s)
Common faults: Bouncing; Rolling to the outside of the foot; Partial range
Progress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Progress by: Single leg, off a step, add load
Regress by: Two legs, hand support, flat floor
Same level swaps: KOT Calf Raise; Single Leg Calf Raise; Calf Raise (Straight Knee)
Joint notes: Achilles pain: slow heavy calf raises are rehab gold.
Default prescription: 3 x 12 to 20 (slow)

Why: The Optimal group burpee: hands down, step back to plank, step in, stand tall. All of the metabolic benefit with no jumping or landing.
Cue 1: Hands down, step or jump back to plank
Cue 2: Chest down (if required), back to feet
Cue 3: Stand tall (jump only if allowed)
Common faults: Sagging plank; Crashing to the floor; Sloppy as fatigue builds
Progress to: SSB Pause Squat (G4)
Progress by: Add a press, push up or jump
Regress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Regress by: Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench
Same level swaps: Squat Thrust to Bench (No Jump); Sprawls; Burpees
Joint notes: IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
Default prescription: 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s

Why: Hands on a bench, step back and in. A no impact, wrist friendly burpee regression for groups and seniors.
Cue 1: Hands down, step or jump back to plank
Cue 2: Chest down (if required), back to feet
Cue 3: Stand tall (jump only if allowed)
Common faults: Sagging plank; Crashing to the floor; Sloppy as fatigue builds
Progress to: SSB Pause Squat (G4)
Progress by: Add a press, push up or jump
Regress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Regress by: Step back burpee, incline burpee onto a bench
Same level swaps: Step Back Burpee (No Jump); Sprawls; Burpees
Joint notes: IMPACT when jumping: group sessions use the no jump version (step back, step in, stand). Devil's press and man makers: DB hinge skill required.
Default prescription: 3 to 6 x 20 to 40s

Why: Step one foot out to the side as the arms rise overhead, alternate sides. Low impact jumping jack alternative for groups.
Cue 1: Light on the toes
Cue 2: Rhythm
Cue 3: Soft knees
Common faults: Heavy landing; Too long; Poor posture
Progress to: SSB Squat (G3); SSB Box Squat (G3); Nordic Curl (Full) (G3)
Progress by: Faster, longer
Regress to: Patrick Step (G1); Elephant Walk (G1); KOT Calf Raise (G1)
Regress by: Step jacks
Same level swaps: Skipping; Star Jumps; Jumping Jacks
Joint notes: IMPACT: excluded from group sessions and avoid with pelvic floor symptoms.
Default prescription: 30 to 60s

Why: Driving the knees up in a fast march with no hop. A no impact swap for high knees in group warm ups and finishers.
Cue 1: Move through big comfortable ranges
Cue 2: Increase range each rep
Cue 3: Breathe and stay controlled
Common faults: Rushing; Bouncing into range; Skipping the warm up
Progress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Progress by: Bigger range, add reaches
Regress by: Smaller range, hand support
Same level swaps: A March; Inchworm; Crab Reach
Joint notes: Safe for almost everyone.
Default prescription: 1 to 2 x 5 to 10 each side (or 20 to 30m)

Exercise: Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski)
Equipment: Assault bike / bike, Rower, Ski erg
Muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
Why: 20 to 45 minutes at a pace where you can just hold a conversation (RPE 3 to 4). Builds the aerobic base, mitochondrial health and fat burning capacity; Peter Attia's longevity foundation. Usually done outside group sessions (walks, cycling) or as recovery.
Cue 1: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Cue 2: Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Cue 3: Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
Common faults: Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals
Progress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Progress by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
Regress by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest
Same level swaps: Rower and Ski Ladder; Sprint Intervals 10 to 20s (Bike or Ski); Rower 500m
Joint notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
Default prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
Coach sources: Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

Muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
Why: 4 to 5 intervals of 3 to 4 minutes hard (RPE 8 to 9) with equal easy recovery on the bike, rower or ski. Improves peak aerobic capacity, one of the strongest predictors of longevity (Attia). Teams, once per week maximum.
Cue 1: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Cue 2: Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Cue 3: Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
Common faults: Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals
Progress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Progress by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
Regress by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest
Same level swaps: Rower 500m; Tabata Bike; Bike (Easy)
Joint notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.
Default prescription: Intervals: e.g. 6 to 10 x 15 to 30s hard / 60 to 90s easy, or 20 to 40 min steady (zone 2)
Coach sources: Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

Muscles: Heart and lungs, legs (bike/rower), upper body (ski/rower)
Why: 6 to 10 all out efforts of 10 to 20 seconds with 1 to 2 minutes easy. Stacy Sims recommends this short, sharp style for peri and post menopausal women; Cosgrove ranks intervals above steady cardio for fat loss. Zero impact on the bike or ski erg.
Variation notes: Fast/power version: move with intent, stop when speed drops.
Cue 1: Bike: push and pull with arms and legs, steady cadence
Cue 2: Rower: legs, body, arms; then arms, body, legs
Cue 3: Ski: hinge and pull down, drive the hips
Common faults: Rowing with the arms first; Hunched posture; Going out too hard in intervals
Progress to: ATG Split Squat (G2); SSB Split Squat (G2); SSB Good Morning (G2)
Progress by: Longer work, shorter rest, higher watts/calories, more rounds
Regress by: Easier pace, shorter intervals, more rest
Same level swaps: Zone 2 Steady State (Bike, Rower or Ski); Tabata Bike; Bike (Easy)
Joint notes: Low impact. Rower and ski: watch low back flexion. Treadmill sprints involve impact.

Coach sources: Attia (zone 2, VO2), Cosgrove (intervals), Stacy Sims (sprints), Ben Patrick (backward walking)

Why: The trap bar lets people stand inside the weight with neutral grip, so the load sits in line with the body. Far less low back stress than a straight bar and much easier to learn. DeFranco and Cosgrove's go to heavy lift and Optimal's default heavy deadlift for 40+ (bone density, strength, grip).
Cue 1: Stand in the middle, hinge down and grip the handles
Cue 2: Chest proud, take the slack out of the bar, brace
Cue 3: Push the floor away, stand tall, lower with control
Common faults: Hips shooting up first; Rounding the back off the floor; Jerking the bar off the floor
Progress to: Rack Pull (G4); Block Pull (G4); Sumo Deadlift (G4)
Progress by: Add load, low handles, pause just off the floor, rep max progressions (Teams G4)
Regress to: Trap Bar RDL (G2); Trap Bar Deadlift (High Handles) (G2); Tempo DB RDL (G2)
Regress by: High handles, KB deadlift from blocks, lighter load
Same level swaps: Trap Bar Deadlift; Paused DB RDL; Barbell Romanian Deadlift
Joint notes: The most joint friendly heavy lift. High handles reduce range for tall members or stiff hips/backs.
Default prescription: 3 to 4 sets x 6 to 10 reps, tempo 3-1-1-0, rest 90 to 120s, RPE 7 to 8

Why: Hamstrings both extend the hip and bend the knee; curls train the knee bending role that RDLs miss. Strong hamstrings protect knees and reduce hamstring strain risk. Nordic curls are among the best researched injury prevention exercises.
Cue 1: Lie on your back, heels on the ball/sliders/TRX, lift the hips
Cue 2: Curl the heels towards the bum keeping the hips high
Cue 3: Extend slowly back out (control is the exercise)
Common faults: Hips dropping during the curl; Rushing the lowering; Cramping (start with fewer reps)
Progress to: SSB Pause Squat (G4); Single Leg Slider Curl (G4)
Progress by: Hips stay up throughout, single leg, slower lowering, Nordic progression
Regress to: TRX Hamstring Curl (G2); Swiss Ball Hamstring Curl (G2); Hamstring Curl (Swiss Ball) (G2)
Regress by: Hips on the floor curl, eccentric only, double leg
Same level swaps: Slider Hamstring Curl; Hamstring Curl (Slider); Single Leg Swiss Ball Curl
Joint notes: Knee friendly. Nordics are demanding: use band assistance and partial range, expect soreness at first.
Default prescription: 3 sets x 8 to 12 reps, tempo 3-0-1-1, rest 60 to 90s, RPE 7 to 9
